ca_butcher_area.blurb: A cut-up boulder beside the loop trail at the far end of the Culp Valley campground, in the San Diego County desert. It holds eight problems, nearly all of them low to moderate: a handful of V0 and V1 lines, plus one V2 and one V3. The block is one of many in a larger boulder field spread across the surrounding hills, so it fits easily into a day of wandering between boulders. Reaching it takes a short hike from the campsites, either along the trail or straight through the brush.

ca_funky_boulders.blurb: A compact jumble of sandstone boulders at Castle Rock State Park in the Santa Cruz Mountains, tucked right beside the trail and next to the larger Nature Boulder. It has eight problems: one very easy line, four around V1, and a few steps up to a V4 crack. Landings are mostly straightforward and the lines are short, slabby or sloper-driven, so it suits newer boulderers or a warm-up stop on a round of the Indian Rock boulders. Parking is at the Indian Rock lot, and the walk in is brief.

ca_white_dike_wall.blurb: A small wall on Donner Summit above Truckee, split by a broad white dike that gives it its name. It faces east and has eight routes, four sport and four trad. Grades centre on 5.9 to 5.11, with one easy 5.6 trad line and a single 5.12 at the top end. Most of the lines are on the short side, so the wall works best as one stop in a day that also takes in the neighbouring Snowshed, Smokeshed or Train Time walls. The approach follows the Snowshed side and finishes with a scramble onto the old rail tunnel.

ca_clapper_boulder.blurb: A single boulder on the West Rim of the Happy Boulders, in the Volcanic Tablelands outside Bishop. It carries eight problems with a very wide spread: one V1, four V2s on slabby ground, and three hard lines from V6 up to V8, including the pinch problem that gives the block its name. The landings are flat, which helps on the harder lines. From the main trail climb to the rim and continue along it until the boulder appears.

ca_banana_cracks.blurb: A steep-faced formation in the Lost Horse area of Joshua Tree National Park, set between Quail Springs Road and Hemingway Buttress. All eight routes are trad crack lines, running from an easy 5.7 up to one 5.12 arete, with the bulk sitting in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. Expect to place your own gear throughout. Park in the large paved Hemingway lot, follow the trail toward Hemingway, then bear right to reach the base.

ca_chuckawalla_boulder.blurb: A low, north-facing boulder in the Outback section of Hidden Valley, Joshua Tree National Park, a short way south of the Iron Door Cave. Its heavily featured face holds eight problems, starting at very easy and reaching V6 on a harder start variation. Most are V0 or V1, with two V4s in the middle of the range for stronger boulderers. A trail leaves Hidden Valley Campground past the east side of The Blob.

ca_cascade_wall.blurb: A sport wall deep in the Monkeyface Falls canyon in the San Bernardino Mountains, with water pouring behind the climbing. It has eight routes covering a wide range, from a 5.3 and 5.4 through a 5.7 and 5.9 to a pair of 5.11s and a 5.12. Reaching it is part of the experience: you drop into the canyon from Dog House Ledge by rope, cross the stream, then hike up. Plan on competence with rappelling and a way out, such as jugging a fixed line or climbing one of the easier routes.

ca_cascade_falls_left.blurb: A trad crag on the west side of Cascade Creek, beside Highway 140 in the lower Merced River canyon of Yosemite. It has eight routes, all placed on natural gear, spanning 5.8 to 5.12: two at 5.8, two at 5.9, a 5.10, a low 5.11 and two 5.12s. Two lines are multi-pitch, one of two pitches and one that stretches to seven. Leave the car at the lot by the Cascade bridge, where the approaches are obvious. In spring the area can be wet.
